title: PR 07 — Login, KV sessions, route guard, and logout
description: Implement the password step of login, opaque KV-backed sessions in an httpOnly cookie, a server guard for `/app` routes, logout, and session revocation. Requirement IDs: TASK-19, TASK-20.
acceptanceCriteria: `POST /auth/login` accepts email plus the client-derived auth hash and returns a generic 401 for both unknown email and wrong password
Server verification uses the stored HMAC pepper and a constant-time comparison
Successful login sets `bw_session` with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age 30 days
KV stores only `sha256(token)` mapped to session metadata; the raw token is never persisted
Unauthenticated access to `/app/*` redirects to `/login` and preserves the intended path
`POST /auth/logout` deletes the KV entry, clears the cookie, and is idempotent
A revoked session cannot be reused even with the old cookie value
The login response returns only post-auth parameters needed by the client (`kdfSalt`, `kdfIterations`, wrapped vault key), never ciphertext items

steps.details: Create `app/lib/.server/session.ts` with `createSession(env, userId, meta)`, `getSession(env, request)`, `destroySession(env, request)`, and `revokeUserSessions(env, userId)`. Store `sess:<sha256(token)>` in KV with JSON `{ userId, createdAt, lastSeenAt, uaHash, ipHash, ver }` and a 30-day expiration. Use a per-user `ver` counter stored on the user row so revocation can invalidate all tokens without listing KV keys.

Create `app/lib/.server/verify.ts` with `hashAuthHash(authHash, serverSalt)` = HMAC-SHA256(AUTH_PEPPER, authHash || serverSalt) and a constant-time compare against `users.auth_hash`. Accept base64url input, reject wrong lengths early without timing differences that distinguish user existence.

Create `app/routes/login.tsx` as a transport-only route plus the page entry `app/features/login/login.tsx` with `index.ts`. On submit, derive `authHash` client-side from the entered password and the KDF parameters fetched for that email. Return `{ kdfSalt, kdfIterations }` from a `GET`-free lookup step or a single POST that returns a generic 401 for unknown email, then a second step posts the hash. Never echo the email back in an error message.

On successful verification, create the session and set the cookie via `Set-Cookie` with the attributes from the acceptance criteria. Refresh `lastSeenAt` at most once per hour to limit KV writes. If a user's `ver` differs from the session's `ver`, treat the session as invalid.

Create `requireUser(request, env)` that resolves the session, loads the user, rejects `status='disabled'`, and throws a redirect to `/login?next=<path>` with the path encoded safely. Apply it to `/app`, `/app/trash`, and all `/api/*` handlers. Return 401 JSON for API routes instead of a redirect.

Create `POST /auth/logout` that destroys the session and clears the cookie. Add an admin-triggered `revokeUserSessions` that increments the user's session version. Include a helper that password change and recovery reset will call in TASK-11.

Vitest: wrong email and wrong password produce the same status and body; cookie attributes are exact; a session with a stale `ver` is rejected. Playwright: login → `/app` reachable; logout → `/app` redirects; visiting `/app` first redirects to login and then back to `/app` after auth.

technicalNotes: Do not store the session token in D1; KV with a hashed key is the design.
KV is eventually consistent; treat revocation via the `ver` column in D1 as authoritative.
Never log request bodies for auth routes.
The client must clear the entered master password from component state as soon as the hash is derived.
2FA is intentionally out of scope; the login response shape must be extensible with `requires2fa`.
